common_mistakes: Starting siding removal before the building permit is issued and posted — Boston can stop the job and require re-submittal
Using a trade permit instead of a building permit — siding replacement is an exterior building scope, not electrical/plumbing/mechanical
Failing to disclose sheathing or framing repairs discovered after demo — that can trigger additional review and delay final approval

response_body.inspection_booking: Schedule inspections through Boston ISD's online permit/inspection system from the Boston.gov Inspectional Services page. Phone: (617) 635-5300. Boston commonly requires at least 24 hours advance notice for inspection requests; book early because exterior work inspections can queue up. Verify the current inspection request method on the ISD portal before calling for a slot.

pro_tips: Use the Short Form Building permit route if the work is truly siding-only with no structural changes; that is usually the fastest path in Boston
Have the exact siding square footage and job value ready before applying — Boston's fee is valuation-based, so an accurate value keeps the permit fee from getting kicked back
If the house is in a historic district, check that siding material and profile are allowed before ordering materials; that is a common delay point in Boston
Take photos of any rotten sheathing or framing before covering it up — inspectors may want proof of repairs if hidden damage is found
